subject: Commercial: consumption safeguards, peak reconciliation & tier ceiling proposal
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.g@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@blueharbor.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial: consumption safeguards, peak reconciliation & tier ceiling proposal

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks for the RFP details — appreciated. Attached is a concise commercial proposal focused on the billing model questions you flagged: commit tiers, handling large short-duration spikes, reconciliation cadence, and protection for multi-workload variability. Key highlights below (attachments: 20270521-bh-commercial-term-sheet-v1.pdf, usage-smoothing-examples.xlsx):

- Baseline commit: annual committed token volume (example: 1.2B tokens) billed monthly as an amortized reservation. Unit price for committed tokens: $0.0009 per token.
- Peak ceiling & short bursts: we propose a Peak Reconciliation bucket that decouples transient spikes (<=72 hours) from month-to-month true-ups. Spikes above 200% of your 7-day moving average are routed to the Peak bucket and capped at a 1.6x surcharge on committed unit price for the first 50M burst tokens per month.
- Overage mechanics: consumption beyond committed + peak bucket is billed at standard overage rate of $0.0016 per token. True-up is performed monthly with an annual reconciliation to apply any credits.
- Graceband & smoothing: a rolling 3-month smoothing window with a 10% amortized credit for underutilization in any single month (applied as invoice credit in the following month).
- Pilot credits: for a 90-day pilot we provide a $50k usage credit and a one-time migration credit of up to $12k for integration and eval costs.
- Discount ladder: multi-year commitments (2-year or 3-year) can receive step-down discounts of 7% and 12% respectively on committed unit price; volume breakpoints escalate discounting at 2B and 5B committed tokens.
- SLA & invoice remediation: latency SLOs with financial credits (details in attachment). Billing disputes can be raised within 60 days; we will provide per-request logs and token-level breakdowns to facilitate reconciliation.

Notes on implementation and operational guardrails: we recommend two model classes for BlueHarbor workloads (high-throughput embeddings for search, and conversational generation for support flows). We will provide recommended batching and KV-caching profiles per workload to help you achieve predictable unit economics.

If this structure looks reasonable, we can prepare a tracked redline of the term sheet and circulate to procurement. Quick question for you: do you prefer monthly true-ups with an annual cap (we defaulted to this) or quarterly true-ups for smoother financial forecasting?

Thanks,
Rafael
Director, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20270521-bh-commercial-term-sheet-v1.pdf (application/pdf), usage-smoothing-examples.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Samir Gupta <samir.g@blueharbor.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@blueharbor.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial: consumption safeguards, peak reconciliation & tier ceiling proposal

Rafael — thanks for the detailed summary and the attachments. A few quick clarifications before we loop procurement: 

1) Peak bucket timing: when you say "<=72 hours" for transient spikes, does that mean any contiguous window up to 72 hours is eligible, regardless of when it occurs?
2) Is the 200% threshold calculated per-route or aggregated at the account level? We have some routes that are often noisy but isolated.
3) For the pilot credit, can unused pilot credits roll into the first invoice if integration runs long?

If those are simple, we'll confirm and request an initial redline.

Samir
Sr. Product Ops
BlueHarbor Financial

On Fri, 21 May 2027 at 09:12, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (original message and attachments)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.g@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@blueharbor.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial: consumption safeguards, peak reconciliation & tier ceiling proposal

Hi Samir — quick answers inline and added Marissa/Ben for pricing nuance: 

1) Peak window: yes — any contiguous window up to 72 hours is eligible, but eligibility is gated by our noise filter (see usage-smoothing-examples.xlsx). If a spike repeats frequently (>3 occurrences/month) we treat it as sustained and it falls back to overage pricing.

2) Threshold calculation: default is account-level aggregation to provide cross-route smoothing, but we can scope it per-route on specific endpoints if BlueHarbor prefers (per-route scope would require routing labels and may reduce smoothing effectiveness).

3) Pilot credit rollover: we can allow unused pilot credits to roll into the first month invoice for projects that enter production within 120 days of pilot end. After that window credits expire.

Marissa: Ben — eyes on the surcharge cap language — Samir asked about applicability to repeated short spikes. Proposed concession: cap the Peak surcharge at 1.4x (instead of 1.6x) for the first 30M burst tokens if BlueHarbor commits to a 24-month term and a minimum 2B annual commit. Thoughts?

Best,
Rafael

> On Fri, 21 May 2027 at 11:03, Samir Gupta <samir.g@blueharbor.com> wrote:
> > Rafael — thanks for the detailed summary...

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Commercial: consumption safeguards, peak reconciliation & tier ceiling proposal

Rafael / team,

I like the concession as a negotiation lever. Quick internal notes: 
- If we reduce the initial peak surcharge to 1.4x for the first 30M burst tokens on a 24-month, 2B commit, we should tighten the repeat-spike clause: allow up to 2 occurrences/month (not 3) before treating traffic as sustained.
- Keep the 72-hour technical window — that's standard.
- For accounting: pilot credit rollover to the first invoice is fine but cap the rollover to 50% of the pilot credit if it transitions to production after pilot >90 days. That prevents gaming.
- Approve per-account threshold by default; offer per-route scoping as an optional add-on (chargeable).

I will update the term-sheet and send a tracked redline to Rafael to share with Samir.

Ben
Head of Commercial Pricing
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: tracked term sheet and next steps

Samir / Priya — thanks for the rapid back-and-forth. Attached is the tracked-term-sheet PDF reflecting the concession language: peak surcharge reduced to 1.4x for first 30M burst tokens on a 24-month, 2B annual commit; repeat-spike tolerance tightened to 2 occurrences/month; pilot-credit-rollover capped at 50% if production start >90 days.

Next steps:
1) Procurement review — we'll accept a single commercial redline and respond within 48 business hours.
2) Legal: we can exchange a short-form MSA with the consumed token mechanics appended as an exhibit.
3) Onboarding: we will schedule a 60-minute architecture + billing workshop to configure routing labels and smoothing profiles.

Please confirm if you want the initial redline template or a clean MSA for signature. Happy to set a call this week.

Regards,
Rafael
Director, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
